answer: Real things have to be carried. Picture a harbor that hands each arriving captain a notary's token: to claim a berth, someone standing on the dock, holding an onyx seal, must countersign the log in person. Digital clones can whisper attestations by the thousand, but this ledger prices every endorsement in travel - a genuine meeting, a witness with a name, a boot print in wet timber at the pier. Forging it means hiring bodies at each port, the one cost a farm cannot scale without leaving fingerprints.
